- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price spikes.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >65), model forecasts often overshoot or fail to peak accurately, then overcorrect downward.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — forecasts show persistent downward bias after peaks, while true prices often stabilize or rebound.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward lower values in the 30-day forecast, particularly when historical prices are above 65.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 10 days, then become more aggressive — suggesting a delayed response to recent price momentum.
- Model fails to capture the “late-stage” price surge (last 5–10 days of forecast) — often underestimates the final 10–15% of the true price range.
- When true prices rise sharply, model forecasts lag by 1–3 days and then overshoot — suggesting a delayed reaction to policy or market signals.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases after a dip — often fails to recognize “rebound” phases after corrections.
